$comment: The buffers of NCode.Buffers, for the picker on /start/which-buffer/ (WhichBuffer.astro, BufferCard.astro) and the matrix on /reference/buffer-behavior/: one data file, so the two cannot disagree. `snippet` is the key of the compiled call the page shows in the card; `evidence` names tests in evidence.json. `anchor` is the card's anchor on /start/which-buffer/. Booleans in `behavior`: true, false, or null where the question does not apply. Text fields take `code` and [links](/x/).

questions.text: Is the data a secret, or derived from one?

answers.text: Yes: a key, a password, a token, a MAC

questions.text: Where does the memory come from?

answers.text: I already have it: an array an API handed me, or a small fixed-size secret in one synchronous method that fits `stackalloc`
I need new memory for it

questions.text: Do you know its length before you start writing it?

answers.text: No: it grows as I write, such as serialized JSON

questions.text: What does the code that uses it need?

answers.text: To cross an `await`, or to live in a field

questions.text: What do you need for it?

answers.text: A fixed-size buffer, written in synchronous code
A fixed-size buffer kept in a field or across an `await`

outcomes.name: `BufferFactory.Rent` with `out Span<T>`
outcomes.use: A temporary buffer for a key, a password or another secret, in synchronous code.
outcomes.watchFor: The span is the length you asked for. `owner.Memory` is the whole buffer, 4096 bytes for a smaller request.

behavior.source: `SecureMemoryPool<T>.Shared` up to 4096 bytes; a pinned array of its own above that
behavior.contents: Not cleared: write before you read
behavior.afterDispose: Zeroed, and back in the pool

outcomes.name: `BufferFactory.Rent` with `out Memory<T>`
outcomes.use: A secret that must cross an `await` or live in a field.
outcomes.watchFor: Do the span work in a synchronous helper. Never keep the `Memory<T>` after its owner is disposed.
outcomes.dispose: The `IMemoryOwner<T>` that `Rent` returns, when the last `await` that uses it is done.

behavior.source: The same pool and owner as the `Span<T>` overload
behavior.contents: Not cleared: write before you read
behavior.afterDispose: Zeroed, and back in the pool

outcomes.name: `BufferFactory.CreatePooledBufferWriter(isSensitive: true)`
outcomes.use: A secret whose length you do not know until you have written it.
outcomes.watchFor: It adds a segment as it grows. To read it as one span, use `GetSpanLease` or `ConsumeAsContiguousSpan` with the same `isSensitive`.

behavior.source: Segments from `SecureMemoryPool<T>.Shared`; a larger segment is a pinned array of its own
behavior.contents: Only what you write is read back
behavior.afterDispose: Every segment zeroed, and back in its pool

outcomes.name: `SecureMemoryPool<T>`
outcomes.use: An API that takes a `MemoryPool<T>`, such as a pipe.
outcomes.watchFor: `Rent` returns a whole buffer: 4096 bytes for any smaller request. Create the pool your application uses, and dispose it when the application stops.
outcomes.dispose: Each `IMemoryOwner<T>` it rents, and the pool when you are done with it.

behavior.source: Buffers of 4096 bytes, cached for reuse; a larger request gets a pinned array of its own
behavior.contents: Not cleared: write before you read
behavior.afterDispose: Zeroed, and back in the pool

outcomes.name: `BufferFactory.CreatePinnedArray`
outcomes.use: An API that takes or fills a `T[]`, within one synchronous scope.
outcomes.watchFor: The array outlives the lifetime: never return it, store it or hand it to a logger. Every call allocates.

behavior.source: A new pinned array of exactly that length
behavior.contents: Not cleared: write before you read
behavior.afterDispose: Zeroed. The array is still there, and still writable

outcomes.name: `GetSecureLifetime()` on a span
outcomes.use: Memory you already have: `stackalloc` for a small secret, or an array an API returned.
outcomes.watchFor: It zeroes; it does not pin. Stack memory does not move, but an array you had may have moved before you wrapped it.

outcomes.name: `Rent` or `CreatePooledBufferWriter` with `isSensitive: false`
outcomes.use: Pooled buffers for data that is not secret.
outcomes.watchFor: Nothing is pinned or zeroed: the next renter can read what you wrote. Never put a secret here.
outcomes.dispose: The owner or the `Sequence<T>`, with `using`, so the buffer goes back to the pool.

behavior.length: Exactly what you asked for, or what you have written
behavior.afterDispose: Back in the pool, as it is

outcomes.name: `BufferFactory.CreateArrayBufferWriter`
outcomes.use: A writer that grows, for output that is never secret.
outcomes.watchFor: Each time it grows it copies into a larger array and drops the old one. Never write a secret into it.

behavior.contents: Only what you write is read back

outcomes.name: `FixedSpanBufferWriter<T>`
outcomes.use: Writing into a fixed-size span, such as `stackalloc`, in synchronous code.
outcomes.watchFor: It cannot grow: asking for more space than is free throws. Pass it by `ref`: a copy is a second writer.
outcomes.dispose: Nothing: it writes into memory you own.

outcomes.name: `FixedMemoryBufferWriter<T>`
outcomes.use: Writing into fixed-size `Memory<T>`, with the writer kept in a field or across an `await`.
outcomes.watchFor: It cannot grow: asking for more space than is free throws.
outcomes.dispose: Nothing: it writes into memory you own.
